heat rejection: the shipped `heat_rejection` block (24 rows) is UNMAPPED against this table and is reported as such, never as corroborated. Its own `notes` cite ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Table 6.8.1G and its `template` column names DOE reference vintages; its `minimum_performance` is an ASHRAE gpm-per-hp figure while this table publishes a fan-power RATIO (electrical kW per thermal kW, e.g. at most 0.013 for a propeller-fan open tower). Two different quantities on two different bases: there is no row-and-column mapping to make. The block is vestigial - the runtime applies the 0.013 ratio separately - so this is data hygiene, not a behavioural item

boiler FHeatPLC: this table writes a fuel-ratio quadratic while the shipped curve is the EnergyPlus efficiency multiplier PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR), compared as functions over PLR 0.10-1.00. Against the requirement each class is actually subject to, the curve its rows are GIVEN deviates by 2.67 % (non-condensing) and 45.54 % (condensing). Equipment-class selection is what makes this large: `hvac/efficiency.py` gives EVERY `boilers` row `BOILER-EFFFPLR` and every `furnaces` row `FURNACE-EFFPLR`, so naming a curve `-COND` does not assign it - no row references either condensing curve. The reference building elects modulating equipment: `hvac/reference.py` represents purchased heating by a gas-fired MODULATING boiler, which receives `BOILER-EFFFPLR` like every other. `BOILER-EFFFPLR-COND`, the curve NAMED for the condensing class, would deviate by only 0.49 % - but no row uses it. Pending D-89

MODULATING boilers and furnaces: this table is now CONSUMED, and it is the largest part-load finding in this edition. It states FHeatPLC as ten printed (PLR, FHeatPLC) points, so the requirement is PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC at each of them. Against it the curve every boiler row is given, `BOILER-EFFFPLR`, deviates by up to 33.51 %, and the curve every furnace row is given, `FURNACE-EFFPLR`, by up to 11.32 %; the snapshot ships no curve named for the modulating class at all. Equipment-class selection is what makes this large: `hvac/efficiency.py` gives EVERY `boilers` row `BOILER-EFFFPLR` and every `furnaces` row `FURNACE-EFFPLR`, so naming a curve `-COND` does not assign it - no row references either condensing curve. The reference building elects modulating equipment: `hvac/reference.py` represents purchased heating by a gas-fired MODULATING boiler, which receives `BOILER-EFFFPLR` like every other. Pending D-89

furnace FHeatPLC: this table writes a fuel-ratio quadratic while the shipped curve is the EnergyPlus efficiency multiplier PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR). Against the requirement each class is actually subject to, `FURNACE-EFFPLR` - which every `furnaces` row is given - deviates by 1.16 % (atmospheric) and 23.25 % (condensing); `FURNACE-EFFPLR-COND`, named for the condensing class, would deviate by 0.49 % but no row uses it. This edition's modulating furnace requirement is Table 8.4.5.2.-B, recorded there. Pending D-89
